canonical_summary: Automated-history and shared Assistant runtime compaction use an idempotent transaction with a frozen input head, current user tail where applicable, compacted artifact hash, retained exact recent tail, semantic-closure check, no-gain detection, and a commit marker. The compacted body is stored as a typed artifact and later admitted by Context Admission rather than silently replacing authoritative history. A failed or interrupted transaction leaves the prior head current; marker recovery, rewind, branching, and tool-result artifact references cannot invent or drop turns. Direct Assistant Chat remains a separate model-aware lane and owns its user-visible behavior.
negative_constraints: Do not mutate canonical history before the compacted artifact and receipt commit atomically.
Do not drop the current user tail, unresolved instructions, exact IDs, corrections, or required evidence.
Do not inject oversized raw tool results into later turns when an authorized artifact reference suffices.
Do not claim compaction succeeded when no useful space was reclaimed.
Do not impose automated-envelope behavior unchanged on direct Assistant Chat.
examples: If compaction crashes after writing a candidate artifact but before the commit marker, recovery keeps the previous history head and treats the candidate as uncommitted; a later retry may reuse it only after exact input-hash validation.
compatibility_only_notes: Assistant Chat visuals and interaction design are external owners; this ledger supplies only shared runtime contracts.
Existing compacted history remains source lineage and must not be retroactively claimed transaction-safe.
gui_classification_reason: The atom defines shared backend compaction, artifact, receipt, and recovery semantics; referenced Chat controls are owned elsewhere.

title: Use deterministic conditional rules for small phase-local instruction deltas
canonical_summary: A versioned deterministic conditional-rule engine may evaluate typed runtime facts and append a small, stable-ID instruction delta only when a preregistered condition applies. Each firing records the rule version, matched fact IDs, emitted instruction IDs, and rendered-byte dependency. The mechanism is program logic, not a model gate or a second reader, and it cannot grant permissions, expand FileSafe scope, change provider/model routing, bypass Context or Packet Admission, or replace core safety instructions. Conflicts fail closed to bounded adjudication before dispatch.
negative_constraints: Do not use an extra model to decide ordinary rule firing.
Do not repeat the whole policy manual when one applicable rule fires.
Do not let evidence or retrieved text define executable conditional rules.
Do not let conditional reminders replace deterministic enforcement or final admission.
Do not mutate provider bytes after final gate approval.
examples: When a typed stage enters external-source synthesis, one registered citation-integrity delta is included and receipted; unrelated build, GUI, and provider rules remain absent.
compatibility_only_notes: `Time-Traveling` is source terminology; canonical Plans may choose a clearer deterministic-rule name while preserving lineage.
stale_retired_terms: repeat all rules just in case
gui_classification_reason: This is backend deterministic rule evaluation, prompt dependency, and admission behavior.

title: Keep BSD as an explicit optional advisor, default-off until qualified
canonical_summary: BSD, if retained, is a separate bounded advisor-model call that can propose a small instruction or recovery delta. It is not Packet Admission, Context Admission, FileSafe, response conformance, or a mandatory second reader. The product default is Off until dedicated evidence shows useful intervention quality, acceptable false-positive and false-negative behavior, bounded usage, and safe failure semantics. Any future Auto mode requires an explicit versioned policy, visible usage attribution, reserved capacity, immutable inputs, typed output, no authority widening, and a deterministic decision about whether its proposal is admitted; On remains an explicit user or workflow choice within authorized scope.
negative_constraints: Do not add a mandatory BSD call to every dispatch.
Do not describe BSD as a deterministic gate.
Do not let BSD grant permissions, choose hidden routes, or rewrite final provider bytes after admission.
Do not enable Auto by default before empirical qualification.
Do not hide BSD cost, provider usage, latency, or failure state.
examples: With BSD Off, the ordinary path still compiles, admits, dispatches, and validates using deterministic services and one assigned worker call. A future explicitly enabled BSD pass returns a typed suggestion that the normal admission path may accept or reject.
compatibility_only_notes: The packet's proposed Auto default is not accepted for the first release because it conflicts with the zero-hidden-reader and usage concerns.
BSD remains a testable optional feature, not removed from future design space.
stale_retired_terms: two models must read every prompt
gui_classification_reason: This atom defines backend optional model-call policy and usage/authority boundaries; any control presentation is owned by separate GUI plans.

title: Recover tool failures through typed bounded envelopes and re-admission
canonical_summary: Tool, MCP, skill, retrieval, attachment, and artifact access use selected progressive capability schemas and a typed Tool Recovery Envelope. Failure classes distinguish unavailable, unauthorized, denied, malformed, timeout, empty, over-cap, stale, partial, and provider-transport outcomes. Recovery offers only preregistered alternatives within current authority, caps model-controlled evidence requests before execution, externalizes oversized results to hashed artifacts, and requires renewed Context/Packet/FileSafe checks whenever the provider-visible request or effective action changes. Hidden semantic retries and unbounded tool loops are forbidden.
negative_constraints: Do not attach every tool, MCP, plugin, or skill schema to every turn.
Do not retry semantically after a failure without a typed transition and current admission.
Do not execute an unbounded list of model-requested evidence fetches.
Do not convert denied access into a different route or wider permission silently.
Do not inline oversized raw outputs into subsequent prompts.
examples: A selected search tool returns over-cap output; the runtime stores a hashed artifact, admits a bounded excerpt and reference, records the terminal distinctly, and rechecks the changed capsule before the worker continues.
compatibility_only_notes: Existing tool retry behavior remains unqualified until it emits the typed envelope and exact dependency receipts.
stale_retired_terms: all enabled tools are always injected
gui_classification_reason: This is backend capability selection, failure typing, artifact handling, and recovery admission.

title: Expose compact resource facts and preserve observable resumable work
canonical_summary: Server, provider, account, model, cache, allowance, process, and RuntimeResourceGovernor state remains durable outside prompts. Each controller or worker receives only the task-relevant compact projection needed to choose among already-authorized routes, concurrency, waves, queueing, or pause states. Required work remains ObservableWork with stable IDs, queued/active/provider-active/wait/reset timing, remaining backlog, receipts, and honest terminals. Resource pressure changes scheduling, not obligation coverage or completion truth. Product runtime contracts remain native typed services; browser automation is test tooling rather than the Puppet Master runtime shape, and SQLite is not introduced by this course correction.
negative_constraints: Do not inject full process, port, provider, usage, or server registries into a model turn.
Do not let temporary allowance or resource pressure erase required work or create false completion.
Do not let a worker choose an unauthorized provider/account/model route from operational data.
Do not equate browser test tooling with production runtime architecture.
Do not add SQLite as an implicit state store.
examples: A planner sees that two authorized routes are available and one is waiting for reset, plus admitted parallelism and remaining waves; detailed credentials, other accounts, process tables, and unrelated usage history remain outside the capsule.
compatibility_only_notes: Existing RuntimeResourceGovernor and Usage contracts should be reused rather than duplicated.
This atom does not redesign Settings, Usage, or server-management visuals.
gui_classification_reason: This is backend resource projection, scheduling, timing, state-store, and runtime architecture.

title: Provide typed runtime receipts to GUI owners without redesigning their concepts
canonical_summary: Context Lens, Compact Now, rewind/branching, thread search/request/spawn, active-turn redirects, Goal visibility, attachment routes, provider/cache warnings, BSD mode and usage visibility if retained, and ObservableWork status consume typed shared-runtime contracts from this architecture. Their user-facing screen, panel, form, layout, styling, component, icon, and interaction design remains owned by the separate Assistant Chat, Settings, Usage, Planning Wizard, and PMConcept7 concept lanes. This ledger may specify exact receipt fields, states, commands, and failure semantics required for truthful presentation, but it must not overwrite those visual concepts or make a visual control grant backend authority.
negative_constraints: Do not redesign Settings, Assistant Chat, PMConcept7, Usage, or Planning visuals in this ledger.
Do not let a visible selection bypass Context Admission, Packet Admission, FileSafe, route registration, or capability checks.
Do not claim a GUI warning or badge is enforcement evidence.
Do not hide unavailable, stale, partial, or unverified runtime state from the owning surface.
examples: A Context Lens panel may display the Context Receipt's included, omitted, compacted, and on-demand blocks; its layout belongs to the Chat concept, while the receipt identity and truth semantics belong to the shared runtime contract.
compatibility_only_notes: Direct Assistant Chat remains outside the strict automated envelope and may change its thread-local model or Persona mid-thread.
This atom is an interface boundary, not permission to edit external concept families.
stale_retired_terms: Chat uses the automated fixed envelope
gui_classification_reason: The atom explicitly defines user-visible GUI consumers such as panels, controls, warnings, status presentation, and interaction surfaces, while preserving separate visual ownership.
